clue.text: Henry's on to a case which causes devastation

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
VOC is the grammatical abbreviation for the vocative case

explanation.surface: A man called Henry takes on a legal case that wreaks destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a lawsuit, but it is the grammatical vocative, abbreviated VOC; Henry's H comes first, on top of A.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread destruction and ruin, the same as devastation.

clue.text: It's senseless to dispose of foreign capital

parts.note: senseless, as in crazy, means mad
to be rid of something is to have disposed of it

explanation.surface: Getting rid of money held abroad would be madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid is the capital city of Spain, foreign from the British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Paradise so long as beasts don't get toothache

parts.note: the Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise
ta-ta is a casual British farewell, like so long

explanation.surface: Heaven lasts only as long as animals are spared dental pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: edentates are toothless mammals such as anteaters and sloths, so they can never get toothache.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentata is the zoological order of toothless mammals, such as sloths and armadillos.

clue.text: Grave nothing! The French take a chance with it

parts.note: a grave is a tomb
nothing is zero, the letter O
la is the French feminine form of 'the'

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark about the grave, then a shrug from the French about gambling.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOMBOLA is a British raffle drawn from a revolving drum at fetes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery in which buyers gamble on drawing a winning ticket.

clue.text: Recollected having been summoned again

explanation.surface: Someone remembered they had been called back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall is both to remember something and to order someone back, as an ambassador or a faulty product.

clue.text: How long does a boxing match last? Too long!

definitions.text: How long does a boxing match last?

explanation.surface: An impatient fan asks how long a fight goes on, then complains it drags.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits as A BOUT TIME, the length of a fight; the second is the exasperated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a boxing match, so its duration is its time; and 'about time' is the cry when something is overdue.

clue.text: Quarrelling pets

parts.note: two familiar household animals give the idiom for people who fight constantly

explanation.surface: Two household animals squabbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight like a cat and dog means to quarrel bitterly, and both are typical pets.

clue.text: Number at Welsh resort

parts.note: ten is a number
by means at or beside, as in 'by the sea'

explanation.surface: A count taken at a seaside town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenby is a seaside town in Pembrokeshire, south-west Wales.

clue.text: Non-clerical member of US city is in charge

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A lay member of the Los Angeles congregation runs things.
explanation.definitionFit: A laic is a layperson, someone who is not one of the clergy.

clue.text: Don Brook creation that is turned by hand

indicators.note: a creation is something made, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A craftsman named Don Brook has made something to be turned by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don Brook' reads like a name; its letters rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A door handle shaped like a ball is rotated by the hand to open the door.

clue.text: Sailor Bill uses half of the old counter

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
AC (account) is a bill

indicators.note: the first half of the word uses is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor pays his bill using half the coins from an old shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a shop's, but here it is a device for counting: beads on wires used since antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is an ancient calculating frame, a device for counting.

clue.text: Legendary works each containing identical Roman figures

indicators.note: the abbreviation for each holds the other letters within it
two identical figures means the same numeral appears twice

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Ancient sagas each hold matching Roman numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a collection of Old Norse poems and prose of myths and legends.

clue.text: Spread all round city an area.

indicators.note: spreading the letters out scatters them into a new arrangement

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A city sprawls outward over a whole region.
explanation.definitionFit: A locality is a neighbourhood or district, a particular area.

clue.text: Appeal to Catherine for approval

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O come'
Kay is a short form of the name Catherine

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with Catherine to give her consent.
explanation.definitionFit: An okay is a go-ahead, an expression of agreement or sanction.

clue.text: Make situation worse for a Girl Guide initially, Virginia, in class

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words are taken
the state's abbreviation sits inside the word for class

parts.note: rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide from Virginia worsens matters in her class.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggravate is to intensify a problem, making it more serious.

clue.text: Drink cocktail, looking wooden

definitions.note: the definition is the material described by the adjective: a hardwood

parts.note: tea is a drink
read as cock-tail, the tail of the word cock, its last letter K

explanation.surface: Someone drinks a mixed drink and looks stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail' looks like a drink, but split as 'cock tail' it gives the last letter of 'cock'.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hard durable timber from a tropical tree, used for furniture.

clue.text: Dame fell over cheese

indicators.note: a tumble jumbles the order of the letters of Dame

explanation.surface: An elderly lady took a tumble over some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coating.

clue.text: The intellectual had for example double trouble

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters are mixed
double means the abbreviation for example is written twice

explanation.surface: The brainy one had, say, twice the problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' writes EG twice, EGEG; 'trouble' mixes that with HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is a highbrow, a bookish person often thought out of touch.

clue.text: Eel sheds constructed despite the dangers

indicators.note: constructed means built anew, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Sheds for eels were built regardless of risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means careless, without paying attention to risk.

clue.text: Account of refined 17 at Yarmouth school

indicators.note: refined means processed, so the cheese's letters are reworked

parts.note: the answer to 17 Down is EDAM
the mouth, or opening letter, of Yarmouth is Y

explanation.surface: A report of fancy cheese served at a seaside school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' rearranges EDAM (17) to ADEM; 'Yarmouth' gives its first letter, Y, its 'mouth'. Yarmouth is an English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a place of learning, a private or specialised school.

clue.text: One who petitions for wild animal caught outside

indicators.note: the abbreviation for caught goes round the rest

parts.note: CT is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A petitioner wants a wild beast that has been trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges ANIMAL to LAIMAN, which sits inside CT.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant is someone who makes a claim, such as for benefits or in court.

clue.text: Little woman left an alcoholic radical

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women

explanation.surface: A small lady departed, a drunken extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' is the chemistry sense: a group of atoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Amyl is the chemical group C5H11, found in amyl alcohol.

clue.text: Cereal food that is eaten by errant males

indicators.note: the abbreviation is swallowed within the other letters
errant means wandering astray, so these letters are moved about

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Wandering men eat some breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'errant' rearranges MALES to MEALS, which takes IE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mealies is the South African word for maize, corn eaten as a staple.

clue.text: Note with regret not all are revolting

parts.note: G is a musical note
to rue is to regret
some means a part, not all

explanation.surface: A message expressing sorrow says not everyone is rebelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like rebelling, but it means disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrifying or repellent, disgusting to see.

clue.text: Admits possessing

definitions.meaning: to confess or acknowledge, as in owning up

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to having something.
explanation.definitionFit: To own is both to have as property and to confess, as in owning to a mistake.

clue.text: Pop group making a come-back unchanged

indicators.note: read backwards the letters stay the same, so the group's name is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A band returns to the stage exactly as before.
explanation.walkthrough: The name reads the same backwards, so a come-back leaves it unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Abba was the Swedish band that won Eurovision in 1974.

clue.text: Cook what a follower could get?

parts.note: B follows A in the alphabet
to raise is to get or obtain, as in raising funds

explanation.surface: A cook wonders what pay rise a disciple might receive.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a pay rise; 'a follower' is the letter after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook slowly in a covered pot with a little liquid.

clue.text: Sounds metal, Rob!

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word for a metal is said aloud

parts.note: steel is a metal alloy

explanation.surface: Rob is addressed about metal noises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like a name being addressed, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rob is to take something unlawfully, to thieve.

clue.text: Island paradise wherein a number take a German title

indicators.note: the title takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: von is the German aristocratic title particle
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A paradise island where numbers of people acquire German nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: AVON takes A and L inside: A + V(AL)ON. Avalon is the legendary island of King Arthur.
explanation.definitionFit: Avalon is the blessed isle of Arthurian legend, an earthly paradise.

clue.text: Thrash, thrash, thrash

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
to baste is to beat soundly

explanation.surface: A threefold command to beat someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word three times: one definition and two synonyms joined.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambaste is to beat severely or criticise harshly.

clue.text: Way to acquire wood store

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
ash is a wood

explanation.surface: A route to obtain timber for storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stash is a hidden supply, a secret store of something.

clue.text: Wendy Sade went berserk yesterday

indicators.note: going berserk means going wild, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Two women, Wendy and Sade, ran wild yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition only holds if today is Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: If today is Thursday, the day before is the midweek day.
